title: Putting a Withdrawn Building Automation Service Plan Back into Service and the Charge It Carries
content:
# Putting a Withdrawn Building Automation Service Plan Back into Service and the Charge It Carries

## The handling

When a building owner asks for an automation service plan under the Building Automation Service Plans that stands withdrawn to be put back into service, the desk restores remote access and alarm monitoring and raises a reinstatement charge on the plan. Remote access and alarm monitoring are restored and the reinstatement charge raised only once the balance owed under the plan stands at nil or below.

## Restoring the plan

The restoration is an agent-side office entry: the desk unlocks the tool `reinstate_controls_plan_58d0efe4` and calls it. One call moves the named plan back to live standing, stamps today's office date as the day service was restored, and books the reinstatement charge on a new office invoice so that what the owner owes under the plan rises by that amount. From then on the owner's engineers can connect to the site again and the monitoring desk watches the site's alarms.

## What is given at the call

| Value | What it is | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_id` | the reference number of the automation service plan being put back into service, read from the automation service plan lookup before the call | an identifier |
| `reinstatement_charge_usd` | the money charged for putting the plan back into service | in USD, recorded positive and to 2 decimal places |

## What comes back

A confirmation sentence in plain text naming the plan restored, the day service was restored, the reference of the booked charge entry, the invoice number it was raised on, the charge in USD to two decimal places and the balance now owed under the plan. The sentence being returned at all is what indicates the plan is live again; no separate status flag is sent back.

## Contract questions

**What standing does the plan hold afterwards?** Live standing, with today's office date stamped as the day service was restored.

**What becomes of the balance?** What the owner owes under the plan rises by the charge booked, and the confirmation names the balance now owed.
